claim: hostedAuthCapable is NOT claimed. This receipt records that `--auth-deployment hosted` now ADMITS on a real served public HTTPS origin under a real signed attestation — superseding the 2026-07-25 refusal witness (hosted-auth-refusal.v0.json) — and that two attested facts are not yet enforced by the origin, and that the LLP 0077 sender-auth matrix did not run. Every leg is recorded below with its exact status.

topology.tlsTerminator: Caddy, in the same network namespace
topology.flyEdgeMode: raw TCP passthrough on public 443 (no `tls` handler), `http` handler on 80 for ACME only
topology.witness: machine log line `snapback listening on http://127.0.0.1:4287` while https://snapback-drill.fly.dev/health returns 200
topology.whyItMatters: LLP 0060 D2's edge-to-origin clause is satisfied literally ('same-host loopback'), and the direct-origin bypass class is empty: no address outside the namespace routes to the origin socket. The LLP 0060 D1 plaintext fence is satisfied by its ordinary loopback rule — no fence was weakened and no sessions override exists.

legs.what: `--auth-deployment hosted` admits on the served origin under a signed, deployment-bound admission verified against the release-bound Ed25519 public key.
legs.evidence: GET https://snapback-drill.fly.dev/health -> 200; the origin composed hosted serving pre-bind and installed the verified authority.

legs.what: The served public origin publishes the tuple carried by its verified admission, not a build constant.
legs.evidence: GET /inspect capabilityManifest.hostedAuth = {externalTls: enforced, effectiveSource: trusted, authenticationThrottle: sharedEnforced, sessionInvalidation: globallyFenced, clientCredentialPosture: senderConstrainedV2}. A local target still publishes the all-negative tuple.

legs.what: The public HTTPS leg uses a publicly trusted certificate obtained by the deployment itself and terminated in-namespace.
legs.evidence: issuer= C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=YE2; subject= CN=snapback-drill.fly.dev; notBefore=2026-07-25, notAfter=2026-10-23. First-contact strict transport is `hstsPreloadedSuffix`: the `dev` TLD is HSTS-preloaded with include_subdomains, verified against hstspreload.org (status `preloaded`, preloadedDomain `dev`), so the hostname is HTTPS-only before first contact.

legs.status: GAP (fixed same day, not yet redeployed)
legs.what: The admission asserts `operatorSurface: "disabled"`, which LLP 0060 C2 defines as a fixed 404 for every `/_snapback/*` page and API route on the public application origin.
legs.observed: GET https://snapback-drill.fly.dev/_snapback/admin -> 503 with an 'Admin Console unavailable' HTML body.
legs.assessment: The origin does not enforce the disablement the attestation asserts; 503 is an incidental unavailability (the admin UI bundle is absent), not a deliberate fixed 404. This is an UNENFORCED ATTESTED FACT and is exactly the overclaim class LLP 0074 forbids. It is ledger row S4 of LLP 0098 §8 and it FAILS. FIXED in-tree after this run; the served machine still runs the pre-fix image, so this receipt records the observed 503.
legs.fix: A hosted deployment now serves a fixed body-free 404 on every SystemStatic/SystemApi route before any handler, regardless of admin token, while /inspect stays reachable. Regression test: hosted_admission_enforces_the_operator_surface_it_attests. Residual: a method-mismatched probe still returns 405 from the router method filter before the gate runs.

legs.what: LLP 0060 D2 requires credential-bearing plaintext to be REFUSED, never redirected; redirects are permitted only for credential-free navigation.
legs.observed: GET http://snapback-drill.fly.dev/health -> 308 redirect. The terminator redirects all plaintext paths uniformly, so a credential-bearing plaintext request would also be redirected rather than refused.
legs.assessment: The terminator's blanket HTTP->HTTPS redirect does not distinguish credential-bearing paths. `externalTls: enforced` is attested but this component of D2 is not enforced.

legs.what: The full LLP 0077 sender-constrained matrix (grant matrix over every grant-presenting route and both carriers, issuance outcome matrix, nonce/anti-oracle axes, replay refusal, WebSocket sender_nonce release) against the served origin.
legs.reason: The deployment's active auth mode is `dev`. Sessions mode is selected by the application schema (`auth: { mode: 'sessions' }`) and requires `--startup-artifacts` on every start plus a two-boot staging transition; this deployment does not yet stage a sessions carrier. Witnessed: GET /auth/session reports activeMode `dev`, and POST /auth/request-code refuses SNAPBACK_AUTH_MODE_DEV ('the session provider is unavailable while auth mode is dev').

legs.what: An admission snapshot lives at most five minutes (LLP 0060 D5), so serving withdraws when the current snapshot lapses.
legs.posture: renewal = presignedWindow: a 48-snapshot chain covering four hours was pre-signed once and delivered as a platform secret; the origin selects the member covering its boot instant. There is no hot-swap renewal loop, so serving withdraws at the end of the window and the control plane cannot withdraw inside it.
legs.assessment: Honest cost of pre-signing, recorded rather than hidden. An `online` renewal mechanism is LLP 0098 open question 1.

platformFindings: This machine has no persistent volume: an auto-stop/start cycle wipes the rootfs, destroying both the delivered admission chain and Caddy's certificate storage, which forces a fresh Let's Encrypt issuance against the 5-per-week duplicate-certificate limit. The profile therefore runs with auto_stop_machines = off and min_machines_running = 1. A volume is the production answer.

Fly raw TCP passthrough on public 443 for a `<app>.fly.dev` hostname works over both the dedicated IPv6 and the shared IPv4 (SNI-routed). Let's Encrypt issued successfully via TLS-ALPN-01 and later HTTP-01 through the passthrough.
claimBoundary: This receipt proves that a hosted-edge attestation now exists, is verified, and admits serving on a real public origin. It does NOT prove the LLP 0077 sender-auth contract on that origin, and it records two attested-but-unenforced facts. hostedAuthCapable remains unclaimed and the LLP 0077 program-index capability gate stays open.
